content.title: 'Shrinking' Producer Bill Lawrence Reveals Why Season 4 Will Start Fresh After Emotional Finale (Exclusive)
content.text: Warning: Spoilers for Shrinking season 3, episode 11, which debuted Wednesday, April 8 NEED TO KNOW Shrinking season 3 concludes the original three-season story arc but sets up a creative reset for season 4Co-creator Bill Lawrence says the show will continue with the same cast and explore new storylines moving forwardThe season 3 theme of "moving forward" is reflected in major character growth and life changes for the ensemble cast Shrinking season 3 has officially come to an end, closing out the story for the first three installments of the Apple TV+ dramedy from co-creator Bill Lawrence. But given the series was renewed for season 4, this is far from the end of series, with the showrunner teasing to PEOPLE that they will introduce a new "beginning, middle and end." Most notably, that means the arc involving Jimmy (Jason Segel) grieving the death of his wife over the past three seasons has been resolved, especially now that the therapist has sparked a new romance with Sofi (Cobie Smulders). During the final moments of the finale, Jimmy is seen sitting down for breakfast with Sofi after Paul (Harrison Ford) tricks him into meeting one last time. Paul, meanwhile, has moved across the country with his wife, Julie (Wendie Malick), to be closer to his daughter, Meg (Lily Rabe). It just so happens he's not far away from where Jimmy's daughter, Alice (Lukita Maxwell), decided to go to college. Not only that, but the episode sees everyone else moving forward — in more ways than one — with Liz (Christa Miller) and Derek (Ted McGinley) jetting off to Spain for a much-needed vacation while Brian (Michael Urie) heads off to Tennessee for his husband, Charlie (Devin Kawaoka). Even Sean (Luke Tennie) decides to move out of Jimmy's pool house and Gaby (Jessica Williams) finally gets engaged to Derrick (Damon Wayans Jr.) — all emphasizing that it's time for Jimmy to move forward with his life and strike out on his own. Wendie Malick and Harrison Ford on 'Shrinking' season 3. Kevin Estrada/Apple TV So if the season 3 finale felt like a series finale, it was on purpose. "Here's why it was intentional," Lawrence, 57, says. "This is what I think is cool about streaming shows. When we pitched this show, we pitched the first three seasons, you know, with a beginning, middle and end to this story. And so, as a writing staff, [co-creators] Jason Segel and Brett Goldstein and I all kind of said, 'Hey, we're gonna write the third season as the end of this three-season story.' Even if the show goes on, you have to do that." So moving forward, "if you picked up the fourth year and we came up on Jason Segel and his character was like, 'You know, I'm still really sad about my wife,' then people would be like, 'Enough already,' " the showrunner continues, explaining that because "TV has changed so much" they tell stories in the chapter-like installments. "I'll use Ted Lasso as an example," Lawrence says, referring to the sports comedy starring Jason Sudeikis that he co-created. After season 3, the series was renewed for a surprise fourth season, which is set to debut this summer. "You can do a story at the beginning, middle and end. And we all love the work so much, I think the characters are so rich that if Apple was like, 'Oh, we'd love to do another beginning, middle and end. Can you tell another story with this group?' It'd be no problem." The TV producer behind other current hits, like Rooster and Scrubs, adds, "Not to shine a spotlight on how old I am, but when this season's over, we'll have done 36 episodes of Shrinking. I think with Spin City we did 101 episodes in the first four seasons. I think we did 9,000 episodes total." Damon Wayans Jr. and Jessica Williams on 'Shrinking' season 3. Kevin Estrada/Apple TV Never miss a story — sign up for PEOPLE's free daily newsletter to stay up-to-date on the best of what PEOPLE has to offer​​, from celebrity news to compelling human interest stories. So going off of that, Lawrence says, "I think there's a hundred more stories to tell. I just think we finished the story of Jimmy getting through the lowest point in his life." In a post on X shared ahead of the finale, he echoed what he told PEOPLE by revealing that season 4 will mark a creative reset for the series. "We are ending the [three-season] story we pitched, so [we] have to a tell a new one in [season 4]," he wrote on April 4, while confirming that the show will still have "the exact same cast." As for how things ended with Gaby and Liz in the finale, both Williams, 36, and Miller, 61, reflected on the journeys their characters went through over the season. "Bill said the theme of season 3 is moving forward… In the beginning, Gaby says that she wants to get more into trauma work and her patient — played by the amazing Sherry Cola — is one of her first forays into that world. And it is something that somehow becomes this kind of catalyst to push Gaby forward into really deciding and committing to opening up her own trauma center," Williams tells PEOPLE. Ted McGinley and Christa Miller on 'Shrinking' season 3. Kevin Estrada/Apple TV Related Stories The actress adds, "I loved Gaby's character arc this season. I think the last two seasons, Gaby's character arcs really grew. But this season as an actor, I had big moments in the beginning of the season, big moments in the middle, big moments with Paul and then a big moment at the end." "I just felt like I could never rest and coast out the rest of the season, which as an actress is, if you love the work, which I love, it's a gift," she says, adding that "I don't know if it gets any better than that." In addition to Williams, Miller also had a standout season as Liz, who had some showy moments throughout. "I loved playing Liz this season," she says. "I think she had so many plates spinning in the air, but I felt it was punctured by little holes of realization and growth and hopefulness." Miller adds, "I root for her, you know. She's so messy and she just makes so many mistakes, but I really root for her and I think she ended on an up note at the end of the season." Shrinking season 3 is now streaming on Apple TV+.
